S25.01.needs: a PDF file uploaded to the library
S25.01.note: The PDF reader is an iframe with data-testid library-pdf-reader; it has no visible label of its own.
steps: Sign in and click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab.
Click a PDF file tile.
Look for a reader inside the product (a frame that holds the PDF, with the file name in the top breadcrumb after Library) and compare with Expected.
S25.01.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a PDF file

S25.02.needs: a plain-text file uploaded to the library
S25.02.note: The same text view is also used in project knowledge files (FilePreviewModal, plain text in a pre block).
steps: Sign in and click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab.
Click a plain-text file tile.
Look for a readable text view inside the viewer (top breadcrumb shows Library and the file name) and compare with Expected.
S25.02.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a .txt file

S25.03.needs: a project with a .md file uploaded
S25.03.note: In the Library viewer a .md file shows as raw text in a pre block, not formatted; only the project preview renders Markdown. The name of the knowledge-files list heading was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Sign in and click Projects in the sidebar.
Open a project that has a Markdown file in its knowledge files.
Click the .md file name in the file list.
Look for formatted Markdown in the preview dialog (headings, lists, not raw # and * symbols) and compare with Expected.
S25.03.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > click a .md file name in its knowledge files

S25.04.needs: a project with a source-code file uploaded
S25.04.note: In the Library viewer source files show as plain text, not syntax-aware; only the project preview highlights code.
steps: Sign in and click Projects in the sidebar.
Open a project that has a source-code file (for example .ts or .py) in its knowledge files.
Click that file name.
Look for the code in a syntax-aware, fenced code block with a language, and compare with Expected.
S25.04.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > click a source-code file name in its knowledge files

S25.05.needs: an image uploaded to the library
steps: Sign in and click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Images tab.
Click an image tile.
Look for the image shown large in the viewer with the file name as its alt text and a Close file viewer button in the top right, and compare with Expected.
S25.05.where: Sidebar > Library > Images > click an image tile

S25.07.needs: a video file uploaded to the library
S25.07.note: The player is a plain HTML video element with the controls attribute; no custom control label was found.
steps: Sign in and click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Videos tab.
Click a video tile.
Look for a video player with playback controls (data-testid library-video-player) and press play, then compare with Expected.
S25.07.where: Sidebar > Library > Videos > click a video tile

labels.text: Showing the start of this file. Download it to see all of it.

S25.08.needs: a spreadsheet file uploaded to the library
S25.08.note: Table output depends on the server returning kind table; which extensions get that was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Sign in and click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab.
Click a spreadsheet tile.
Look for a table with a header row and cells, and for the note Showing the start of this file when the file is long, then compare with Expected.
S25.08.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a spreadsheet file (.csv or .xlsx) tile

S25.10.needs: a .docx file uploaded to the library
S25.10.note: The library viewer shows extracted text in a plain pre block, not the Word layout; the server extracts the text (apps/web/lib/server/office-document-text.ts).
steps: Sign in and click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab.
Click a .docx file tile.
Look for the document's text in the viewer and compare with Expected.
S25.10.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a .docx file tile

S25.14.needs: an image uploaded to the library
S25.14.note: Zoom controls appear only for images; the zoom group is labelled Zoom.
steps: Open an image in Library as in S25.05.
Note the percentage shown between the zoom buttons (starts at 100%).
Click Zoom in and look for the image getting larger and the percentage rising.
Click Zoom out and check it shrinks back, then compare with Expected.
S25.14.where: Sidebar > Library > Images > click an image tile > Zoom in or Zoom out (top right)

S25.25.note: No full-screen control was found in the Library viewer, the project file preview (FilePreviewModal) or the library components; the only Enter fullscreen and Exit fullscreen controls are for artifacts in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx, not files. Searched for full-screen, fullscreen and requestFullscreen in those folders.

S25.26.needs: a file uploaded to the library
S25.26.note: The Library download is an icon with the aria label Download plus the file name; the project preview has a text Download button.
steps: Sign in and click Library in the sidebar.
Click a file tile that opens a viewer.
Click the Download icon at the top right of the viewer.
Open the downloaded file and compare its bytes and content with the source file, then compare with Expected.
S25.26.where: Sidebar > Library > click a file tile > Download icon (top right, labelled Download with the file name)

S25.27.needs: a .docx file uploaded to the library
S25.27.note: The button is icon-only with title Download as text; it appears only after the text preview is ready and the file is not already text. The downloaded file type was not confirmed beyond a text/plain blob at LibraryView.tsx line 1132.
steps: Sign in and click Library in the sidebar.
Click the Documents tab and open a .docx file.
Hover the top-right icons and find the one whose tooltip reads Download as text.
Click it, open the downloaded file, and compare with Expected.
S25.27.where: Sidebar > Library > Documents > click a .docx file tile > Download as text icon (top right)

S25.28.note: No copy control or selection handling was found in the library viewer, FilePreviewModal or KnowledgeFilesPanel (searched for copy, clipboard, selection and user-select). Browser text selection may still work but was not confirmed in the code. The ledger says this needs the live web.

labels.text: Preview is not available for this file type.

S25.30.needs: a project with a file that has no preview, such as a .zip
S25.30.note: The Library viewer shows Preview isn’t available for this file inline. with a Download to view button instead, and offers no Open option in either place.
steps: Sign in and click Projects in the sidebar.
Open a project and click a file that cannot be previewed, such as a .zip.
Look for the text Preview is not available for this file type. with the file's type under it.
Look for the Download button and compare with Expected (the text does not offer Open).
S25.30.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > click a file that has no preview (for example a .zip) > Download
